studies.label: Within-subject laboratory experiment: personalized versus standard GAI on Product Improvement Tasks

counts_source.quote: Each of the 62 students engaged in two creativity tasks: one with standard GAI (ChatGPT-4) providing generic feedback, and the other with a personalized GAI tutor (Mr. Ranedeer),

arms.name: Personalized GAI (Mr. Ranedeer)
arms.description: Custom GPT-4 tutor on the Explore GPTs platform: students set learning preferences and co-design a learning plan, receive Socratic-style questions, and obtain goal-aligned feedback and strategic prompts for solution elaboration. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 380), Sect. 3.2.1.

arms.name: Standard GAI (ChatGPT-4)
arms.description: Standard ChatGPT-4 gives broad suggestions in response to student queries, followed by solution generation on further input, supporting open-ended exploration with minimal structure. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 380), Sect. 3.2.1.

studies.task: Students individually propose three original and useful product-improvement solutions per task for a stuffed bunny and a portable coffee machine, using a different assigned AI configuration for each task.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4 and Mr. Ranedeer, both built on OpenAI’s GPT-4 model
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 380), Sect. 3.2.1; model release year not stated

studies.shared_sample: c246: Chen et al. (2026), Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback: Effects on creative problem-solving and feedback uptake, doi:10.14742/ajet.11512. Shared participants are inferred from matching sample characteristics, tools, tasks, procedure, task times, and identical creativity means, SDs, and p-values. Neither report explicitly cross-identifies the other. Treat as one sample for deduplication; these reports must not contribute independent primary estimates for the same question and comparison. Verified against c246 PDF pp. 4–5 (printed pp. 168–169), Participants; pp. 8–9 (printed pp. 172–173), Procedure/Fig. 3; and p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 2.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Quality is the extent to which a solution addresses the task objective. Two trained raters blinded to condition rated the solutions on a five-point Likert scale (worst to best); final scores averaged the two raters. The chapter does not describe how the three solutions per task were combined. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 382), Sect. 3.4.1.

sources.quote: Each of the 62 students engaged in two creativity tasks: one with standard GAI (ChatGPT-4) providing generic feedback, and the other with a personalized GAI tutor (Mr. Ranedeer),

sources.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 383), Sect. 4.1, quality result
sources.quote: personalized condition for quality (M = 3.50, SD = 1.00) than in the standard condition (M = 3.08, SD = 1.12; p = .001; r = .42).
Differences between conditions were examined using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests,

estimates.notes: Paired crossover contrast across both task rounds; no first-round-only results are printed. The same students received both AI configurations. Participant counts use the full crossover sample stated in the Abstract; Sect. 4.1 gives no outcome-specific analysis count and no participant exclusions are reported. The participant unit follows the within-subject design, but aggregation across solutions is unspecified; consequently the level of the printed SDs is left null. The chapter names Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests but prints no signed-rank statistic, z statistic, degrees of freedom, SE, CI, paired-difference SD, or cross-condition correlation for this outcome. se_basis is not_reported because the analysis unit underlying precision cannot be confirmed. The reported r is retained with its printed sign; its formula and standardizer are not stated. No effect, mean difference, or uncertainty has been computed. Exact printed numeric formatting is preserved in the source quotation.

open_items: The chapter does not state how the three solutions per task were combined into the scores analyzed, or explicitly identify the level of the reported SDs. Participant is the design-based unit, but participant-level standardization and precision require clarification.

No outcome-specific analyzed counts, first-round-only summaries, signed-rank or z statistics, paired-difference SDs, cross-condition correlations, SEs, or CIs are printed for the creativity contrasts. Do not compute paired precision from the available marginal SDs alone.

The effect-size formula and standardizer for the reported r values are not stated. The related c246 Table 2 reports different r values despite matching arm means, SDs, and p-values; neither source explicitly explains or corrects the discrepancy. Retain the c041 statistics with their own provenance pending clarification.
The release year of the specific GPT-4 tools is not printed; ai_tool.year remains null.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-09. The entire c041 markdown conversion was read through the references; it has no appendix or supplement. All cited c041 PDF pages were checked with pymupdf text extraction. All estimate statistics come solely from c041 Sect. 4.1. The related report was consulted for design and sample provenance, not to add or replace chapter statistics; it is not a supplement. Its local PDF is C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Chen et al (2026) - Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback.pdf. The c041 chapter says only that tool order was counterbalanced (PDF p. 6, printed p. 381, Sect. 3.3). The lab_rct classification and randomized counts follow the reconciled screening decision using c246 PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Fig. 3, whose allocation box states "Random assignment of feedback sequence". That page was text-extracted and the figure was visually inspected in memory. The counts in this file represent the same crossover participants in both arms, rather than separate groups. The printed full-sample count supports the analyzed counts; no participant exclusions are reported, but outcome-specific counts are absent. Country comes from c246 PDF p. 4 (printed p. 168), Participants: "A total of 62 Chinese university students (41 female) from a normal university participated in the study." The c041 chapter alone does not state country. Product/task mapping is corroborated by c246 PDF pp. 8–9 (printed pp. 172–173), Procedure/Fig. 3. The shared-sample link remains an inference from the matching reports. No preregistration or primary creativity outcome is stated. No overall creativity composite, cross-person diversity outcome, or unassisted post-AI outcome is reported.
